reasoning: Reproduced on the rebuilt bundle: set Settings > Location to lat -33.9 / lon 74.0, opened Weather, tree reads 'panel: Updated 20668 days ago' (one more than the original 20667 because the date rolled from 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-03 - exactly what an epoch-0 sentinel predicts). DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)' with WeatherStatus.lastUpdate declared non-nullable, so the card's guard 'if (widget.lastUpdate != null)' at weather_status_card.dart:240 can never be false. Also note the state is not transient: with no network it persists for the whole session.

title: Dismissing a blocking readiness item hides it while the summary keeps counting it, so the panel claims 3 blockers and lists 2
reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle. Equipment > STATUS rail read 'Ready to image / 2 items are blocking first light.' over rows Critical devices (red), Capture output folder (red), Plate solver (amber). Clicked the X on 'Critical devices'; the row vanished, 'Show 1 dismissed' appeared, and the summary STILL read '2 items are blocking first light.' with exactly one blocking row visible. Exact numbers differ from the claim (2/1 instead of 3/2) only because I had set an observing location, which cleared one blocker; the mismatch is identical. Source confirms: readiness_panel.dart:168-173 filters dismissed items out of the rendered rows, while the subtitle counts report.blockedItems.length unfiltered.
location_wrong: Partially. The lying count string is equipment_readiness_panel.dart:68-71 (_subtitle), NOT readiness_panel.dart - this usage passes showHeader:false so readiness_panel.dart's own _summaryDetail (:254-274) never renders. readiness_panel.dart:168-173 is the other half (the dismissal filter), so the cited file is only half the fix; a fixer sent there alone would edit dead code.

title: Readiness panel reports a green "Profile devices — every device is connected" over an empty profile with nothing connected
reasoning: Reproduced live: profile 'My Equipment' with '0 devices' / 'No devices assigned', status bar reading Camera Disconnected / Mount Disconnected / Guider Disconnected, and the full readiness dialog renders 'Profile devices - Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.' Source is unambiguous: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/readiness/readiness_models.dart:369-379, _buildProfileDevices returns ReadinessLevel.ready (green) whenever offlineProfileDevices.isEmpty, with no branch for 'the profile assigns nothing at all'. offlineProfileDevices is built in readiness_provider.dart:105-112 from offlineProfileDeviceNamesProvider, which is empty for an empty profile - the vacuous-truth case the claim describes.
location_wrong: Yes. The claim points at packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/readiness/readiness_panel.dart, which only renders items it is handed. The text, the level and the missing empty-profile branch are all in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/readiness/readiness_models.dart:369-392 (with the input computed at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/readiness_provider.dart:105-112).
reasoning_severity: Downgraded P2 -> P3: the row is misleading over an empty set, but in the same panel 'Critical devices' correctly blocks on the disconnected camera and the summary correctly reads 'Not ready / 2 items are blocking first light', so the panel as a whole never claims the rig is ready.

title: Shell equipment indicator reads "0/0 — No devices configured" while four devices are connected
reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle. Session-connected Simulated Camera, Mount, Focuser and Filter Wheel from Equipment > Discovery. Same frame: header 'panel: 4 connected - 4 unsaved', four Connected device rows, status bar pills 'Camera / Simulated Camera', 'Mount / Simulated Mount', 'Focus / 25000' - and the shell chip 'My Equipment 0/0'. Clicking the chip gives a popup whose entire body is the single line 'No devices configured'. Source: _countConnectedDevices (:91-112) requires profileDeviceId != null so a session-only connection can never be counted, and the else-branch guard at :167 (!hasAnyDevice && connectedCount == 0) then suppresses every per-device row in favour of the 'No devices configured' literal at :173. Location correct.

title: 'Disconnect All' stays enabled and silently no-ops when nothing is connected
reasoning: Source is decisive: the 'Disconnect All' PopupMenuItem at equipment_status_indicator.dart:325-343 takes no `enabled:` argument at all, so it is unconditionally enabled regardless of connectedCount, and _disconnectAll (:453-468) only surfaces a message for summary.failures - a disconnect-all over zero connected devices produces no failures and therefore no feedback of any kind. Confirmed live that the item renders in the popup and is selectable. CAVEAT on the claim's stated evidence: 'the accessibility tree reports button: Disconnect All with no [DISABLED] state' is NOT probative - the sibling 'No devices configured' item has enabled:false in source and also reports with no DISABLED flag, because a disabled PopupMenuItem is not focusable and the harness only emits DISABLED for focusable/selectable/checkable nodes (drive_linux.py:387-389). The finding stands on source, not on that tree line. LIVE CONFIRMATION: with the four simulated devices disconnected (status bar: Camera/Mount/Guider Disconnected), reopened the equipment chip - popup showed 'My Equipment 0/0', greyed-italic 'No devices configured', and a normal-weight 'Disconnect All'. Clicking it closed the menu, the app log stayed at exactly 155 lines before and after, no toast appeared in the tree, and nothing changed.
reasoning_severity: Downgraded P3 -> P4: cosmetic affordance polish. The action is harmless when it no-ops and the popup directly above it already states 'No devices configured'.

title: Slew dropdown drives the mount 69 degrees BELOW the horizon and reports 'Slew complete'
reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle. Site set to lat -33.9 / lon 74.0, Simulated Mount connected and unparked, RA 5.59 / Dec 22.01 entered in Imaging > Mount > GoTo/Sync, split-button menu > 'Slew'. No prompt of any kind. Mount Status then read RA 05h 35m 24.0s, Dec +22 00' 36.0", Alt -23.15 deg, and the toast read 'Slew complete'. I recomputed the altitude independently rather than trusting the readout: with LST ~22.6h, HA = LST - RA = 17.04h = 255.6deg, sin(alt) = sin(22.01)sin(-33.9) + cos(22.01)cos(-33.9)cos(255.6) = -0.209 - 0.191 = -0.400 -> alt = -23.6 deg, matching the app's -23.15 for the slightly later LST. The magnitude differs from the claim's -69.14 only because LST differs; the target is unambiguously under the ground either way. Source: mount_command_service.dart:179-206 slewTo validates only coordinate RANGE (_equatorialCoordinateError) and then unconditionally returns CommandActionResult.success('Slew complete'); _preflightCentering (:345-376) checks camera/centering/solver but never altitude either, so no path in this widget gates on horizon.
location_wrong: Minor line drift only: _handleSlew is at slew_dropdown_button.dart:212-224, not :209-222. The characterization ('calls mountService.slewTo with no altitude precondition; only the centering paths run _preflightCentering') is accurate, though note _preflightCentering does not check altitude either, so fixing it there would not close the gap.

title: Connection troubleshooter says it 'couldn't pin down the exact cause' while holding an error that names the exact cause, then gives four irrelevant hardware steps
reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle. Equipment > Discovery > GUIDERS > Connect on 'Built-in Multi-Star Guider' opens 'Connection help' with headline 'The connection didn't complete' and body 'The guide camera connection didn't complete and we couldn't pin down the exact cause.' The four steps are verbatim as claimed: reseat the cable / confirm power, close other programs holding the guide camera, restart Skotiq, read the raw error. Expanding Technical details in the SAME dialog shows: 'Failed to connect built-in guider: Operation failed: Built-in guider requires an active profile with a guide focal length' - a fully-specified first-party configuration error. My run hit the sibling branch of the same preflight (missing profile focal length) rather than the claim's exact focal_length_mm=0 string, but the classification outcome is identical. Source: _classify in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart:279-318 matches nothing in _configurationMarkers (:263-274 = 'invalid value', '0x80040401', 'value not set', 'not set', 'invalid operation', 'invalid while parked', 'misconfigured', 'bad request') for a message about guide focal length, so it falls through to DiagnosticCategory.unknown, whose headline (:337) and copy (:417) are the 'couldn't pin down' text. The advice is worse than nothing here: the built-in guider is a software guider that reuses the imaging camera and has no cable and no power.
location_wrong: Yes. The classification and the knowledge base are NOT in packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/troubleshooter/connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart (that file only renders). They live in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart - _classify at :279-318, _configurationMarkers at :263-274, _headlineFor at :324-339, and the 'couldn't pin down' sentence at :417.

title: 'Resume' on the incomplete-session dialog is indistinguishable from 'Decide Later' - nothing in the UI shows the session, and it re-prompts identically on the next launch
reasoning: The central assertion does not hold. I ran the controlled A/B the original finding never ran. Seeded imaging_sessions id=1 'NGC 7000 run' status='active' with 14 captured_images, launched, got the identical 'Incomplete Sessions Found' card (14 exposures / 1h 10m total / HFR: 3.20 / 1 failed). RUN A - clicked Resume: Analytics > Session rendered header 'Current Session' / 'Started: Aug 3, 2026 15:30' with a live-ticking DURATION 01:32:22, EXPOSURES 14/0, INTEGRATION 1h 10m, MEDIAN HFR 3.20. RUN B - relaunched and clicked Decide Later: the SAME tab rendered 'Reviewing' + selector chrome and header 'NGC 7000 run' / 'Mon Aug 3, 2026 - 15:30 - active' with DURATION 0s. Those are different code paths: session_tab.dart:39-41 computes isLive = sessionState.isActive && sessionState.dbSessionId == reviewSessionId, and only the isLive branch (:58-68) emits 'Current Session'/'Started:'. So recoverSession's SessionState(isActive: true, ...) IS rendered by a desktop surface, and Resume is observably distinct from Decide Later. WHAT IS STILL TRUE, and worth refiling as its own narrower finding: the Dashboard still reads 'No run active', the top strip 'Idle / No Target', the status bar 'Idle', 'Last run' still 'No runs yet - your first night will appear here', and the prompt DOES recur identically on the next launch (verified: relaunched after Resume and the same card came back unchanged) because recovery lives only in memory. That residual is a P3 'recovery does not survive a restart / dashboard does not reflect it', not the filed P2 'Resume does nothing observable'.
location_wrong: The cited lines are correct as far as they go (session_recovery_dialog.dart:229 _recoverSession, session_provider.dart:228 recoverSession setting SessionState(isActive: true) at :237-247), but the conclusion drawn from them - 'which no desktop surface renders' - is false: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/analytics_screen/session_tab.dart:39-68 renders exactly that state.
